subject: Finalize Q3 OKR Scores, Retros Narrative & Leadership Handback
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 scoring - raw scores + immediate asks

Good morning team — attaching the raw scoring workbook for the Q3 OKR pass. This is the consolidated spreadsheet with per-initiative evidence links and the contested/appeal flags from the adjudication calls. Two quick asks from me before I hand up to the exec packet at 5pm PT:

1) Marissa — please confirm the product evidence row for "Quality regression detection" (it shows 0.6 -> leadership suggested bump to 0.75). I need the specific metric (tests/day, false positive delta) we used for the bump.
2) Ben — engineering to confirm whether the "infra latency" SLO miss is mitigation-only or if we will accept a lowered score given announced infra changes. If mitigation, add the wartime action and ETA.

Notes in the workbook: contested_marks tab (rows with "APPEAL"), and a short draft narrative in the "handback-start" tab. Attachments: Q3_OKR_raw_scores.xlsx; service-reliability-evidence.pdf.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Strategy, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 scoring - raw scores + immediate asks

Thanks Irene — reviewed the contested row. Short answer: evidence supports the bump to 0.75 but with a clarifying caveat.

Details:
- Metric we used: end-to-end regression detection precision over the ops sample (windowed monthly). Baseline was 0.62; after the fallbacks and new evals we observed a median lift to 0.77 for the flagged corpora.
- Artifact: see service-reliability-evidence.pdf pages 4-6 (sample sizes, scripts).

Request: keep the score at 0.75 but add the sentence in the narrative that the improvement is concentrated in <10% of corpora and that ongoing work is required to generalize. That keeps the score recognition but sets expectation and mitigations.

Attaching: small excerpt added to the handback doc (handback-narrative-v1.docx).

Marissa
Director, Product
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Irene/Marissa — quick update from infra. The infra latency SLO miss was driven by a scheduler regression that we patched mid-quarter; the patch plus the planned kernel upgrade gave an observed 35% median improvement in synthetic p95s.

Recommendation: accept a partial score (0.6 -> 0.68) rather than full restoration to 0.8 because the kernel upgrade is still behind canary (expected completion in 3 weeks). If leadership wants full credit now, we can provide a mitigation playbook and a rolling verification plan but I'd prefer the conservative adjustment.

I've added a short mitigation timeline into the workbook and attached the verification snippet into service-reliability-evidence.pdf.

Ben
VP, Infrastructure
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks team — this is a great, pragmatic conversation. My steer for the handback to the execs:

- Approve product's request to keep the 0.75 mark for regression detection, but include the caveat that generalization work is in the roadmap and we'll re-evaluate in 6 weeks.
- Accept Ben's conservative uplift to 0.68 for infra latency with the requirement that we publish the verification plan and daily p95 telemetry to the exec console during the canary. If the canary completes earlier, we will auto-promote the score.

Operational asks (assigned to Irene):
- Update the handback narrative to call out the two conditional moves above.
- Create a one-slide risk summary that will go to the QBR council (internal + Acme rep) with the mitigation ETA and owner.

Irene: if you can update and send the leadership-ready packet to laura by 3:30pm PT, I'll sign off before we forward to the QBR council.

Vivek
COO, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Irene/Vivek — thank you. I reviewed the updated workbook and the narrative v1. Approving the approach with two editorial requests:

1) Tone: change the phrasing in the narrative from "partial recovery" to "conditional restoration pending canary verification" — this reads better for customer-facing QBR materials.
2) Add one line under the Acme-facing slide that calls out potential business impact (small risk to peak inference SLA during major customers' data sweeps) and our plan to prioritize their namespaces during the canary.

Irene: once you send the leadership packet with those edits, I'll add the exec cover note and forward to the QBR council (cc'ing Acme: alex.taylor@acme.io).
